newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to drift before long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to drift before long weekend.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to drift weakly in the Friday session ahead of the three-day weekend, brokers said, as market participants liquidate their positions.
They said that as stocks had posted hefty gains in recent sessions, a correction was expected.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average rose 124.21 points or 0.65 percent to close at 19,275.33. Its June futures were 50 higher at 19,300.
"The Nikkei average ended Thursday with gains but far below the intra-day high and the profit-taking moves may continue today," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager, said.
Brokers said that U.S. payrolls data due out later on Friday and its effect on Wall Street would also heighten the wait-and-see mood in Tokyo.
But they added that the results of the British general election which should be out later today would have little or no direct effect on the Tokyo stock market.

"Tokyo markets don't resume until Tuesday," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "Investors are a bit worried about what could happen in the U.S. markets on Friday, not to mention Monday, and are opting for the sidelines."
Market sources said interest in the U.S. jobs data was eclipsing that in the outcome of the British elections, which were not seen as factor with the potential of influencing Tokyo stocks directly.
After the morning session ended, British Prime Minister John Major, leader of the Conservative Party, conceded defeat.
